title: Travel events
summary: Small things that happen on the way, for the road, the forest, the mountains and the sea. Some rows only fit the day or the night.

tables.name: Travel event: any terrain
tables.description: Picks a terrain and draws an event from it. The road comes up most often.

tables.name: Travel event: road
rows: A toll booth stands where there was none last year. The keeper has a new hat and a bad temper.
A farmer's cart has lost a wheel. He offers a meal and a night in the barn to anyone who helps.
A line of pilgrims walks barefoot on the verge and sings out of tune.
A milestone has been turned around, so the distances on it now belong to the other direction.
A traveling peddler wants to trade stories for news. His last story was about a very large pig.
The road is blocked by a herd of sheep and one very confident dog.
A patrol rides past, looks long at the party and does not stop.
A signpost has been repainted with fresh, cheerful lies.
Someone left a small bundle by a milestone: [[1d4+1]] days of food and a note that says thank you.
A wedding party on its way to the next village invites everyone along, and means it.
A hooded rider asks for the way and thanks everyone too much.
The road forks at an old oak. Someone has carved a very detailed argument into the bark.

rows.text: Campfires glow far off the road in the dark. They go out one at a time as the party comes closer.
A farmer is out in the field at dawn and waves. He seems to be talking to his scarecrow.

tables.name: Travel event: forest
rows: The path ends at a fallen tree as wide as a house. Going around takes an hour.
A stream has flooded a stretch of the trail, ankle deep and very cold.
A hunter's snare lies across the path, set to catch something much smaller than a person.
Every bird falls silent at once and starts up again a moment later.
Half buried by the path lies something small: {{trinkets}}
A colony of mushrooms in a perfect ring glows faintly. Nobody wants to step inside.
A woodcutter's camp, empty, with the fire still warm and an axe stuck in a stump.
A fox follows the party for an hour at a polite distance.
An old shrine to a forgotten spirit has fresh flowers on it.
A swarm of harmless but extremely loud insects drowns out all talk for a while.
Rain starts, but under the thick canopy only a few drops arrive, one at a time and very cold.
A rope bridge over a ravine looks old but holds. Somebody has recently repaired it.

rows.text: Pale eyes shine from the dark between the trees and keep pace with the party until the light returns.
Sunbeams fall through the branches in long golden bars. The forest feels almost kind.

tables.name: Travel event: mountains
rows: A rockslide has covered the path. Climbing over takes [[1d3]] hours and a lot of patience.
A narrow ledge needs a rope and steady nerves. A goat watches and looks unimpressed.
The wind picks up and carries the smell of snow, although the sky is clear.
An abandoned shepherd's hut offers shelter, with a stack of dry wood by the door.
A pass is marked with a cairn of stones, each one with a name scratched into it.
A thin waterfall falls over the path. Behind it is a dry ledge that would hold a camp.
An eagle circles over the party for a long while and then flies off to the north.
A tunnel bored through the rock saves a day of travel but smells strongly of old smoke.
A bridge of ice has formed overnight over a gully and will not last long in the sun.
The echo of the party's voices comes back changed, as if someone were answering from far away.
A lone traveler comes down the pass the other way and warns of mist higher up.
A hot spring steams in a hollow. The water is just right and the view is very good.

rows.text: A thin mist rolls down into the valley after dusk and makes it hard to tell where the path ends.
The sunrise lights the highest peaks gold and pink. For a moment everyone stops walking.

tables.name: Travel event: sea
rows: The wind drops and the sails hang limp. The crew starts to sing and tells everyone to be patient.
A school of silver fish leaps alongside the ship for an hour. The cook is delighted.
A floating crate bobs in the swell. It contains nothing but wet straw and a very angry crab.
A fog bank closes in and the lookout starts to talk to himself.
A ship passes in the far distance and does not answer the signal flags.
A storm builds on the horizon, black and far away, and the captain steers around it with a frown.
A seabird lands on the rail and refuses to leave, however many times it is asked.
The ship's cat has had kittens in somebody's bunk. Nobody dares move them.
A shoal appears on no chart and the helmsman swears it was not there yesterday.
A whale breaches off the starboard side and everyone on deck says nothing at all for a minute.
The water turns a strange green for a mile and then clears again.
A tired messenger bird lands on deck with a message tube for a different ship.

rows.text: The sea glows with a pale blue light around the hull, and the wake looks like a trail of stars.
A bright morning with perfect wind. Spirits on board are high and the crew is generous.
